title: Telemetry-driven spiral rollout for LTS and minor updates
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Design and implement a telemetry-driven 'spiral' progressive delivery system for LTS and minor runtime releases. The spiral pattern ramps traffic outward in concentric cohorts (internal -> power users -> regional cohorts -> global), with adaptive step sizes determined by real-time telemetry signals (error rate, 99th latency, model quality drift). Implementation includes a rollout policy DSL, per-cohort feature-flagging hooks, compatibility checks for LTS channel constraints, and an automated rollback scorer that combines signal divergence, user impact, and trend velocity.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout DSL supports declarative spiral cohorts with per-cohort traffic percentages and hold/exit conditions
Adaptive ramping algorithm reduces or pauses ramps when configured signals exceed thresholds (error rate, p99, quality-drift)
Feature flag integration allows per-customer/tenant cohort assignment and immediate circuit-break for flagged cohorts
Automated rollback scorer produces a single numerical score and a recommended action (continue/hold/rollback) exposed as an event to the Console
Compatibility check prevents promotion to LTS channel if breaking migration hooks are detected
End-to-end e2e test runs in staging simulate a spiral rollout and validate rollback on injected faults
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, and DX; agreed on spiral cohort names and initial telemetry signals (5xx-rate, p99-latency, response-drift-score)
2026-02-25: Prototype DSL v0 posted (see PR), initial simulation shows stable behavior for standard traffic shapes; flagged need for per-tenant throttle config
2026-03-02: Added LTS compatibility validator; discovered edge case where migration-hook timeouts cause false positives — working on debounce logic
2026-03-08: Rollout engine integrated with feature-flag service; first internal canary run executed across night shift cohort, observed expected pause on spike; preparing runbook
2026-03-10: Auto-rollback scorer thresholds tuned after chaos tests; documenting Console event surface for operator actions
notes: This approach focuses on progressive exposure patterns tailored to customers by risk profile. Spiral rollouts help reduce blast radius for wide-surface changes (config migration, KV cache layout updates) while allowing faster promotion when telemetry is healthy. Next steps: finalize DSL syntax, add per-tenant pause-and-retry semantics, and ship an operator-runbook with examples. Consider checklist for legal/regulatory customers that must opt into LTS promotions explicitly.
